entry.title: Rockstar Games Issues Updated Modding Guidelines Ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI Release
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Rockstar Games has updated its modding rules for its entire catalog, including Grand Theft Auto V and Red Dead Redemption II, in anticipation of the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI. The guidelines prohibit modders from mixing assets, characters, or storylines between different Rockstar titles and forbid modifications to the games' established continuity.

Monetization is restricted to the studio's official Creator Platform, with strict prohibitions against real-money gambling, loot boxes, and cryptocurrency. The rules also forbid the use of unauthorized third-party intellectual property, voiceover recordings, and real-world likenesses.

entry.title: Matt Greer Develops Eridin for GBA and PC Using Unified Codebase
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | mattgreer.dev | discussion

Eridin, a fantasy turn-based strategy game, is being developed for both the Nintendo Game Boy Advance (GBA) e-reader and PC to mitigate manufacturing risks. This dual-platform target addresses the difficulty of producing the high-precision dot-strip cards required for reliable e-reader scanning.

The engine uses a single C codebase with an abstraction layer for platform-specific assets, employing DevKitPro and libtonc for GBA and SDL2 for PC. While the PC version maintains the 240x160 GBA resolution, it features subpixel scrolling and uncapped framerates for smoother visual performance.

entry.title: Marvel's Wolverine Allegedly Censored for LGBTQ+ Content in Certain Regions
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Versions of Marvel's Wolverine released in certain regions, specifically cited as the Middle East, have reportedly been stripped of LGBTQ+ content. Users have documented instances where references to the marriage between characters Mystique and Tyger—including in-game photographs, audio, and subtitles—were blurred, muted, or replaced with asterisks.

This follows a precedent by Sony and Insomniac Games, who modified Marvel's Spider-Man 2 to remove pride flags and specific character subplots for distribution in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. These changes align with regional laws in those countries regarding the depiction of homosexuality.

entry.content:
Lobsters Top | unsung.aresluna.org | discussion

The version 5 update of CleanShot has significantly degraded the usability of its settings interface. By attempting to mirror the design language of macOS Ventura and Sequoia, the software has lost the intuitive "shape coding" and efficient layout present in version 4.

Issues identified include a cumbersome two-pane layout, difficult-to-read right-aligned controls, and reduced clicking precision due to narrower interface elements. The design sacrifices functional scannability and accessibility in favor of a modern, system-consistent aesthetic.

entry.title: OpenGOAL Project Offers Native x86-64 Port of Jak and Daxter Trilogy
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | opengoal.dev | discussion

This initiative utilizes a native x86-64 architecture rather than emulation to provide improved performance, accuracy, and compatibility for the original trilogy. By rebuilding the games to mimic the original GOAL programming language, the port ensures gameplay accuracy and compatibility with modern hardware.

The project maintains the original visual and gameplay experience while introducing modern accessibility and quality-of-life features. Because the games are decompiled, the codebase supports extensive modding and provides a foundation for community-created content and technical study of the original game architecture.

entry.title: Using Specific Design Styles to Create Diverse AI-Generated Event Posters
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | john.hartnup.uk | hacker news

Generic AI prompts for event posters often produce repetitive and predictable "twee" aesthetics. By instructing models like ChatGPT to utilize specific design languages—such as Bauhaus, Memphis, or Japanese minimalism—users can bypass default stylistic templates to generate significantly more varied and visually striking layouts.

The experimentation demonstrates that providing precise aesthetic descriptors helps move AI-generated content away from common "craft fair" motifs toward more curated and professional-looking designs. The article also suggests that leveraging models capable of generating editable formats like HTML or SVG can provide even more control for professional designers.

entry.title: King Workers Set to Strike Over Collective Agreement Dispute
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Union workers at King, the developer of Candy Crush, are scheduled to strike on September 25, 2026, if negotiations for a collective agreement fail. The Swedish trade union Unionen, representing a large proportion of the workforce, submitted the strike notice after more than a year of failed discussions.

Other Swedish trade unions, including Naturvetarna and DIK, have announced sympathy strikes in support of the action. King's management maintains that current employment terms are competitive and has declined to enter into a collective bargaining agreement.

entry.title: Typst 0.15 Adds Variable Font Support, MathML, and Bundle Output
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | lwn.net | source | discussion

Typst version 0.15 introduces several significant capabilities, including support for variable fonts that allow continuous weight and style adjustments. It also includes experimental MathML support for HTML exports, a "bundle" feature for generating multiple interlinked output files from a single source, and the ability to manage multiple bibliographies within one document.

The update also expands support for PDF standards, allowing users to target multiple accessibility and archival standards simultaneously. While these features enhance Typst's utility for scientific and technical publishing, its widespread adoption as a LaTeX replacement faces challenges due to the entrenched reliance on legacy formats in academic and professional publishing workflows.
